gen-dafont-azonix-gf-yaldevi: Azonix has wide-mouthed capitals barely taller than its lowercase, with no swelling in any outline, so words take a beat to knit together. Yaldevi sans loosens things up with oversized lowercase.
gen-dafont-bebas-kai-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and friendly, its caps hugging the lowercase height. Bebas Kai stands over it, packed into compact lines with the pressure of a technical pen, so the serif gets more room to breathe across a full paragraph.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-abeezee: Chunky, pencil-drawn and a little squat. ABeeZee follows with terminals that stop well short of the stem, and the plain sans stays easy to scan beside Blockletter's tall, belly-heavy forms.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-aldrich: Blockletter's tall midsection bulges like a squat brush-pen belly. Aldrich, a plain sans with cupped round letters and tall lowercase, gives that heading something steady to stand on.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-alexandria: Blockletter draws every tail and terminal as thick as its stems, which gives headings real weight. Alexandria sans does the opposite job, with open c shapes and short stems that make running text feel light.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-amiko: Amiko sans reads with crayon-tall lowercase and terminals that flare outward like tongs. But Blockletter does the shouting, a skeleton outline held to one fixed stroke, while Amiko does the explaining.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-bangla: Blockletter's strokes have the steadiness of a drawn string. Anek Bangla sans-serif takes over for the actual reading, its wide s curves and short rise to the ascender keeping things easygoing where the heading makes a statement.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-devanagar: Blockletter looks like bent paperclip wire, every stroke the same with no swelling anywhere along it. Anek Devanagari sans-serif adds open mouths and a tall middle zone, which makes the pair feel crisp.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-gujarati: Blockletter holds one unit-width stroke from end to end, like pencil lines that never press harder. And Anek Gujarati, a plain sans, can go a touch larger than usual, since its lowercase already rivals the capitals.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Anek Gurmukhi fills its small letters with big open counters and generous round curves, so it feels breathable at once. Shrink Blockletter too far and its pen-plotter smoothness gets lost.
